content.value_statement: Population-scale single-cell queries can exceed memory or produce duplicated counts. This skill provides focused, reproducible query patterns for CELLxGENE Census analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains Census collections, organism experiments, metadata fields, and expression layers.
Builds cell and gene filters using CELLxGENE value filter syntax.
Shows focused AnnData retrieval patterns for cell types, tissues, diseases, and genes.
Plans out-of-core processing with axis queries and incremental statistics.
Connects Census data with Scanpy analysis and PyTorch training workflows.
Applies primary-data filtering, version pinning, and query-size checks.
limitations: Requires the CELLxGENE Census Python package and network access to Census data.
Does not include Census datasets or execute analyses by itself.
Examples may require updates for the installed Census API version.
Does not validate experimental design, normalization choices, or biological conclusions.

use_cases.title: Explore Tissue Cell Types
use_cases.description: Create a metadata-first query that counts unique cell types within a selected tissue.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan versioned Census retrieval with focused columns, primary-cell filtering, and memory controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare Training Data
use_cases.description: Design filtered Census datasets and batched loaders for cell classification experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a CELLxGENE Census query for primary human B cells from lung tissue. Return cell type, disease, donor, and assay metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Marker Genes
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a versioned Census query comparing CD4, CD8A, and FOXP3 expression across primary T cells from lung and liver.

prompt_templates.title: Process a Large Cohort
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an out-of-core workflow for primary brain cells. Estimate query size, select required columns, process expression batches, and calculate incremental means.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Training Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible PyTorch cell-type classifier using Census data. Prevent donor leakage, define train-test splitting, batch loading, versioning, and evaluation.

output_examples.input: Find unique primary cell types available in human lung tissue.
output: Open a pinned Census version within a managed context.
Query human cell metadata for lung tissue and primary cells.
Select only the cell-type field, then count unique values.

output_examples.input: Compare selected immune marker genes across lung and liver.
output: Confirm gene availability before loading expression values.
Filter primary immune cells and both tissues in one focused request.
Return an AnnData object with tissue, donor, disease, and assay metadata.

output_examples.input: Analyze a brain query that will not fit in memory.
output: Count matching cells before requesting expression data.
Use an axis query and iterate through sparse expression batches.
Update statistics incrementally and release Census resources after processing.

best_practices: Pin a Census release for every reproducible analysis.
Filter primary data unless duplicate cells are the research target.
Estimate result size and select only required metadata and genes.
anti_patterns: Do not load broad expression matrices before checking cell counts.
Do not mix Census versions within one analysis.
Do not assume every dataset measured every requested gene.

faq.question: What data can this skill help query?
faq.answer: It covers human and mouse Census metadata, raw gene expression, dataset presence, and selected integration workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill download data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides query and analysis guidance. Execution requires the Census package, network access, and suitable compute resources.

faq.question: Why filter primary data?
faq.answer: Primary-data filtering avoids counting cells that appear in multiple Census datasets.

faq.question: How should large queries be handled?
faq.answer: Estimate cell counts first, reduce columns and genes, then use axis queries with batched processing.

faq.question: Can it support Scanpy and PyTorch?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include AnnData, Scanpy, and experimental PyTorch workflow patterns.

faq.question: Does it guarantee scientifically valid results?
faq.answer: No. Researchers must validate study design, normalization, confounders, model evaluation, and biological interpretation.
